neutral_facts.value: The accused and the victim were neighbors with a history of animosity. The victim was assaulted at night by a group of 13 individuals. The sole eyewitness, PW1, initially made generalized allegations in the FIR but later provided more specific details in court. The victim sustained multiple injuries, including an incised wound, which the court found improbable to have been caused by only two accused. The eyewitness's credibility was questioned due to inconsistencies in her statements and the unusual circumstances of her reporting the incident alone at an unearthly hour. The prosecution relied on the eyewitness's testimony and the nature of the injuries to establish the assault, but the court found the evidence insufficient to convict the accused due to the presence of multiple assailants and the questionable reliability of the sole witness.

The court also questioned the reliability of PW-8 as an eye-witness due to his absence at the time of the occurrence.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that PW-1 and PW-8 were eye-witnesses to the occurrence, and that appellant no.2 made the fatal assault on the head of the deceased with a lathi while appellant no.1 also assaulted the deceased. They emphasized the existence of a street light and the credibility of PW-1 as an eye-witness due to her relationship with the deceased.

defence_argument.value: The defence submitted that once the other accused have been acquitted, the two appellants alone cannot be convicted with the aid of Section 149 of the Indian Penal Code. They argued that there is no evidence of any common intention, and that PW-1 and PW-8 were not eye witnesses as they reached the scene after the occurrence.
